A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AGN population is very heterogeneous and that the classification of AGN is not a simple matter.
the X-ray data of the Lockman field, combined with the optical/near IR data, show a strong excess of obscured AGN at low redshift and a strong deficit at high redshift.
there are two populations of AGN: one is the classical type 1 AGN, which has a high X-ray to optical ratio, and the other is a type 2 population, which has a low X-ray to optical and near IR ratio.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are two AGN populations, with the same average spectral shape, but different column densities, that are mixed in the hard X-ray band at faint flux levels.
the AGN in the Lockman Hole are not well represented by a single population, but rather by a mixture of type 1 and type 2 AGN.
the X-ray spectral properties of AGN are strongly dependent on redshift and that the AGN population is heterogeneous.
